query: Earlier studies reported high hardness and compressive strength in AlCrCuFeNiTi, CuFeNiMnTi, and low-density AlCrFeTiX high-entropy alloys. However, some AlCrFeTiX alloys were brittle at 25 °C, and AlCrFeTiCo showed only 1.8% plastic strain at 600 °C. Because these findings concern different alloy systems, they do not explain the deformation behavior or the relatively low hardness and strength of equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in its simple solid-solution state, despite its favorable plasticity and machinability. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs this combination of deformation, hardness, and strength and why? Define a controlled comparison that would distinguish the proposed explanation, predict observations relative to the starting alloy, state the composition, state, temperature, and loading limits of the hypothesis, identify the prior evidence supporting its premise, and specify results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The relatively low hardness and strength but high ductility of as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is governed by the absence of B2-ordered Ti–Ni nanoprecipitates. In its simple solid-solution state the alloy cannot overcome the nucleation barrier for ordering, so dislocations glide and cross-slip unimpeded, giving low work hardening. If B2 nanoprecipitates are induced by aging, they will obstruct dislocation motion, raise strength and hardness, and reduce ductility, directly testing the role of order-precipitation strengthening.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, equimolar Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Ni0.2Ti0.2 high-entropy alloy, single-phase FCC matrix, no detectable second phases, average grain size ≈50 µm.
generation.intervention: Isothermal aging at 600 °C for 10 h followed by water quench.
generation.conditions: Uniaxial compression at 25 °C, strain rate 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹.
generation.structural_mediator: ≈10 vol % B2-ordered Ti–Ni nanoprecipitates (~10–50 nm diameter) coherently embedded in the FCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: Coherent B2 precipitates introduce local lattice strains and modulus mismatch that impede dislocation glide and cross-slip, elevating critical resolved shear stress and work hardening rate.
generation.predicted_outcome: Aged alloy exhibits ≥30% higher Vickers hardness and ≥200 MPa higher compressive yield strength, with ≥10% reduction in uniform strain compared to as-cast.
generation.baseline: As-cast CoCrFeNiTi: Vickers hardness ≈2.0 GPa; compressive yield strength ≈500 MPa; uniform compressive strain >40%.
generation.boundary: Applies to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, temperatures between 25 °C and 600 °C, under compressive or tensile loading up to ~1 GPa.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; kinetics of B2 nucleation and stability window in this composition are not yet characterized.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi and age half at 600 °C for 10 h; use TEM and XRD to detect B2 nanoprecipitates; perform hardness and compression tests on both sets at 25 °C under identical conditions.
measurements: TEM quantification of B2 precipitate size and volume fraction
XRD detection of B2 superlattice peaks
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If aging does not produce measurable B2 nanoprecipitates or if hardness and yield strength do not increase by ≥30% and ≥200 MPa respectively (and/or uniform strain does not decrease by ≥10%) relative to as-cast, then the hypothesis is falsified.
